text.p: These are significant stories in the Nigerian press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Commonwealth delegation due in Nigeria on November 19 and 20 for talks with the military government, sources at Commonwealth secretariat in London say.
- Tax exemptions for donors to 400 million naira UNICEF appeal fund to boost child survival programme in Nigeria.
- Nigerian Liquefied Natural Gas company to earn 28.5 billion naira from interests on funds placed in its escrow accounts abroad and chartering of its vessels.
- Government and state-run Nigeria National Petroleum Corporation yet to agree on crude oil price on which to base 1997 budget revenue projections, official sources say.
- Cargo traffic at Tin Can port in Lagos rose by 35 percent in January-September 1996 from year ago period.
- Government favours indigenous firms in bid for marginal oil wells which multinationals find unprofitable but which smaller oil firms want to tap, official sources say.
- Presidency orders 500 buses from Anambra Motor Manufacturing Company to boost its mass transit programme, says an official of the company at the on-going Lagos trade fair.
- Shell and Chevron oil firms begin cost evaluation of local refineries being offered for sale by Nigerian government to see if they should bid for them, company officials say.
